newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian teachers strike closes most public schools.
newsitem.headline: Haitian teachers strike closes most public schools.

text.p: Some 16,000 disgruntled Haitian teachers went on strike on Monday to seek higher pay, closing public schools across the country.
Some teachers have not been paid for as many as two years and are working in schools that lack basic necessities such as running water, toilets and desks, a union spokesman said.

"The base salary for teachers is only about $100 per month," said Andre Lafontant Joseph, secretary general of the National Confederation of Haitian Educators. "It is not enough to live on even when you do receive a paycheck."

He said the union was seeking a meeting with Education Minister Jacques Edouard Alexis before parliament voted on the national budget, which could be as early as next week. Alexis, who was in the countryside, was unavailable for comment but ministry officials said they hoped to set up a meeting with union leaders on Tuesday.
Haiti, which is mired in a chronic budget crisis, has been hit by a wave of strikes in recent weeks across all sectors of society, including hospital workers.
